entry.name: TouchBench
entry.title: TouchBench: Can Vision-Language Models Feel Invisible Physical Properties?
entry.summary: 900 egocentric clips (75 min) of five people wearing a right-hand tactile glove with 132 pressure taxels (60 fingertip, 72 palm), 5 finger-flexion channels and a wrist IMU at about 98 Hz while probing properties hidden from the camera (bottle fill level, cap tightness, ball inflation, pillow filling, cable seating) over 11 tasks, with 900 absolute and 4,102 relative vision-language questions.
entry.hand: tactile glove, right hand (maker not stated)

sensor.note: 137 channels per sample: 132 pressure taxels (60 on fingertips, 72 on the palm) and 5 per-finger flexion values, plus a wrist IMU quaternion; median rate 98.5 Hz.

scale.text: 900 clips (152, 216, 182, 142 and 208 per participant), 75 min, 11 tasks, 5 participants; 900 absolute and 4,102 relative questions

entry.access: The paper gives no release statement, project page or data link (arXiv v1 read in full, 2026-11-25).
caveats: The glove maker and model are not named.
Models are given 32 uniformly spaced frames per clip; the stored video frame rate and resolution are not stated.
The paper's 20 h in-the-wild experiments use the existing EgoTouch corpus, which is not part of TouchBench.

tracking.note: 5 per-finger flexion values; the flexion sensor type is not stated

sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2611.26883 (glove channels, rate, clips, participants, tasks, objects, questions; read to the end)
unconfirmed: hours 1.25 is the paper's 75 minutes of manipulation.
Camera mount 'head' follows the paper's 'head-mounted egocentric camera'; the camera model is not named.
'language' in modalities: the release would pair clips with question and answer text; how it would be stored is unknown.
